title: Abramovich Aides Backdated Documents to Hide Assets and Avoid Taxes, Report Says
text: Abramovich Aides Backdated Documents to Hide Assets and Avoid Taxes, Report Says Oct. 12, 2026 Roman Abramovich. Sergei Kiselev / Moskva News Agency Aides to Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich, including employees of accounting firm Deloitte Cyprus, allegedly backdated more than 1,000 documents to conceal assets and help his businesses avoid taxes, according to an investigation published Monday. The Guardian and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism examined corporate records from the Cyprus Confidential leak, a collection of more than 500,000 documents that includes internal correspondence. The investigation describes an alleged scheme spanning at least 1999 to 2013, in which documents for more than 100 companies linked to Abramovich were backdated, sometimes by as much as five years. Deloitte Cyprus signed off on financial statements based on those records, the report said. Abramovich and his longtime aide Eugene Tenenbaum deny wrongdoing. The investigation identified Tenenbaum and Demetris Ioannides, the former chairman of Deloitte Cyprus, as central figures in the alleged arrangements. title: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks
text: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks Oct. 12, 2026 Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev. Sergei Kiselev / Moskva News Agency Russia is working on measures to protect data centers from drone attacks after a series of “unprecedented” strikes on tech giant Yandex’s facilities, Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev said Monday. “Yandex faced an unprecedented attack. The Digital Development Ministry, together with the Defense Ministry, is working on the issue of protecting these facilities,” Shadayev told a State Duma committee, according to Interfax. He did not specify what protective measures were under consideration. His comments follow drone attacks on three Yandex data centers in four days that have caused server outages that triggered service disruptions for users. The strikes hit facilities in the Ryazan, Kaluga and Vladimir regions between Thursday and Sunday. The disruptions affected Yandex’s ride-hailing, food delivery and payment services, as well as companies that rely on Yandex Cloud, including online retailer Wildberries and fast-food chain Vkusno i Tochka. news Russia’s Yandex Says Data Center in Vladimir Shut D

title: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees
text: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees Oct. 12, 2026 Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Russia plans to open rehabilitation centers in all eight of its federal districts for soldiers who lost limbs in the war in Ukraine, the Vedomosti business daily reported Monday, citing the state-run Defenders of the Fatherland foundation. The foundation did not give a timetable for opening the facilities. The first center is already operating at a Russian State Social University site in the Moscow region and has served 650 veterans. Deputy Defense Minister Anna Tsivilyova, who has been reported to be President Vladimir Putin’s cousin, said the center teaches former soldiers how to use prosthetic limbs in everyday life. One participant told Vedomosti that veterans learn to walk with prostheses and take part in adaptive sports. But some arrive without a finished prosthesis or with one that no longer works, he said. The man, who was mobilized in 2022 and lost his entire right leg at the front, said he now uses ropes to secure his broken prosthesis to his body so he can practice walking. news After Losing Limbs to War, Russian Amputee Veterans Grapple With Officials’ Empty Promises

title: Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing
text: Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing Oct. 12, 2026 Ukrainian service members launch a drone. REUTERS / Valentyn Ogirenko Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia on Monday of violating an “energy ceasefire” announced by U.S. President Donald Trump, urging Washington to ensure Moscow abides by the agreement as the Kremlin said contacts over a possible truce were ongoing. Russia attacked gas production facilities belonging to Ukraine’s state oil and gas company Naftogaz in the Kharkiv region overnight, causing a fire and damaging critical equipment, the company said Monday. Ukrainian drone attacks, meanwhile, appeared to spare Russian oil refineries overnight after Trump made the surprise announcement that the ceasefire had taken immediate effect. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Monday that contacts over a possible energy ceasefire were continuing. He declined to say whether it would apply only to oil refineries, saying further information would be released in due course. “There were Russian violations of the energy ceasefire announced by President Trump,” Zelensky told a security conference in Warsaw via video

title: Rostov Oil Terminal Burns for Third Day After Reported Ukrainian Drone Attack
text: Rostov Oil Terminal Burns for Third Day After Reported Ukrainian Drone Attack Oct. 12, 2026 exilenova_plus / Telegram A fire at an oil terminal in the southern Russian city of Rostov-on-Don continued to burn for a third day Monday after a reported Ukrainian drone attack over the weekend, according to independent media and Ukrainian monitoring channels. Footage published by Astra and Exilenova+ showed flames and thick smoke rising from the terminal’s fuel storage tanks. The facility, owned by the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery, has a total storage capacity of 60,000 cubic meters and can handle 3.5 million metric tons of petroleum products a year, according to publicly available data. Authorities had not announced that the fire had been extinguished as of midday Monday. The Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova said preliminary information indicated that seven of the terminal’s 12 tanks had burned and another showed signs of fire damage. Footage it published showed blackened tanks alongside others still engulfed in flames. The reported extent of the damage could not be independently confirmed. news Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing Read

The officer, identified as Yekaterina F., 30, is a deputy supervisor of local district police officers who has served for at least nine years. title: Abramovich Aides Backdated Documents to Hide Assets and Avoid Taxes, Report Says
text: Abramovich Aides Backdated Documents to Hide Assets and Avoid Taxes, Report Says Oct. 12, 2026 Roman Abramovich. Sergei Kiselev / Moskva News Agency Aides to Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich, including employees of accounting firm Deloitte Cyprus, allegedly backdated more than 1,000 documents to conceal assets and help his businesses avoid taxes, according to an investigation published Monday. The Guardian and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism examined corporate records from the Cyprus Confidential leak, a collection of more than 500,000 documents that includes internal correspondence. The investigation describes an alleged scheme spanning at least 1999 to 2013, in which documents for more than 100 companies linked to Abramovich were backdated, sometimes by as much as five years. Deloitte Cyprus signed off on financial statements based on those records, the report said. Abramovich and his longtime aide Eugene Tenenbaum deny wrongdoing. The investigation identified Tenenbaum and Demetris Ioannides, the former chairman of Deloitte Cyprus, as central figures in the alleged arrangements. title: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks
text: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks Oct. 12, 2026 Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev. Sergei Kiselev / Moskva News Agency Russia is working on measures to protect data centers from drone attacks after a series of “unprecedented” strikes on tech giant Yandex’s facilities, Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev said Monday. “Yandex faced an unprecedented attack. The Digital Development Ministry, together with the Defense Ministry, is working on the issue of protecting these facilities,” Shadayev told a State Duma committee, according to Interfax. He did not specify what protective measures were under consideration. His comments follow drone attacks on three Yandex data centers in four days that have caused server outages that triggered service disruptions for users. The strikes hit facilities in the Ryazan, Kaluga and Vladimir regions between Thursday and Sunday. The disruptions affected Yandex’s ride-hailing, food delivery and payment services, as well as companies that rely on Yandex Cloud, including online retailer Wildberries and fast-food chain Vkusno i Tochka. news Russia’s Yandex Says Data Center in Vladimir Shut D

title: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees
text: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees Oct. 12, 2026 Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Russia plans to open rehabilitation centers in all eight of its federal districts for soldiers who lost limbs in the war in Ukraine, the Vedomosti business daily reported Monday, citing the state-run Defenders of the Fatherland foundation. The foundation did not give a timetable for opening the facilities. The first center is already operating at a Russian State Social University site in the Moscow region and has served 650 veterans. Deputy Defense Minister Anna Tsivilyova, who has been reported to be President Vladimir Putin’s cousin, said the center teaches former soldiers how to use prosthetic limbs in everyday life. One participant told Vedomosti that veterans learn to walk with prostheses and take part in adaptive sports. But some arrive without a finished prosthesis or with one that no longer works, he said. The man, who was mobilized in 2022 and lost his entire right leg at the front, said he now uses ropes to secure his broken prosthesis to his body so he can practice walking. news After Losing Limbs to War, Russian Amputee Veterans Grapple With Officials’ Empty Promises

title: Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing
text: Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing Oct. 12, 2026 Ukrainian service members launch a drone. REUTERS / Valentyn Ogirenko Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia on Monday of violating an “energy ceasefire” announced by U.S. President Donald Trump, urging Washington to ensure Moscow abides by the agreement as the Kremlin said contacts over a possible truce were ongoing. Russia attacked gas production facilities belonging to Ukraine’s state oil and gas company Naftogaz in the Kharkiv region overnight, causing a fire and damaging critical equipment, the company said Monday. Ukrainian drone attacks, meanwhile, appeared to spare Russian oil refineries overnight after Trump made the surprise announcement that the ceasefire had taken immediate effect. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Monday that contacts over a possible energy ceasefire were continuing. He declined to say whether it would apply only to oil refineries, saying further information would be released in due course. “There were Russian violations of the energy ceasefire announced by President Trump,” Zelensky told a security conference in Warsaw via video

title: How has the European Union’s major recovery plan benefited the 27 member states?
text: Advertising How has the European Union’s major recovery plan benefited the 27 member states? Europe The 27 member states of the European Union agreed in July 2020 on a €750 billion post-Covid recovery plan called NextGenerationEU. Its main instrument is the Recovery and Resilience Facility, through which the European Commission has already disbursed €450 billion out of €573 billion. The programme is due to come to an end in a few months. The Commission is currently assessing Member States’ claims for the remaining funds. text: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says Image source, EPA Image caption, Emergency services responded to a Russian drone strike on a residential building in Kharkiv, north-eastern Ukraine on Monday By Olivia Ireland Â and Â Ella Kipling Published 12 October 2026 Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities hours after US President Donald Trump announced the two countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire, Volodymyr Zelensky has said. Despite Trump stating on Sunday the truce would be "effective immediately", the Ukrainian president said Russia had hit "our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities". There were blackouts in the city of Izyum after a Russian strike destroyed power grids, Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform said, while energy and railway infrastructure in western Ukraine was also targeted overnight. On Monday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Ukraine does not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring. What's behind Trump's energy ceasefire claim? Europe Issued on: 12/10/2026 - 12:26 Share The Paris Motor Show opens its doors today, and with it come mounting economic and diplomatic issues. The European Union has just announced that it has secured a commitment from China to moderate the flow of hybrid vehicles into the block's market. title: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees
text: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees Oct. 12, 2026 Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Russia plans to open rehabilitation centers in all eight of its federal districts for soldiers who lost limbs in the war in Ukraine, the Vedomosti business daily reported Monday, citing the state-run Defenders of the Fatherland foundation. The foundation did not give a timetable for opening the facilities. The first center is already operating at a Russian State Social University site in the Moscow region and has served 650 veterans. Deputy Defense Minister Anna Tsivilyova, who has been reported to be President Vladimir Putin’s cousin, said the center teaches former soldiers how to use prosthetic limbs in everyday life. One participant told Vedomosti that veterans learn to walk with prostheses and take part in adaptive sports. But some arrive without a finished prosthesis or with one that no longer works, he said. text: Watch: What could Trump's energy ceasefire mean for Ukraine? Watch: What could Trump's energy ceasefire mean for Ukraine? Close US President Trump said in a social media post on Sunday that an energy ceasefire had been reached between Ukraine and Russia that was "effective immediately". Ukraine's President Zelensky responded by saying his country is willing to back an energy ceasefire if Russia does the same, adding it could "become a major step toward ending the war". However, Moscow hasn't confirmed its agreement and Zelensky said Russia hit a Ukrainian power plant in Kharkiv "immediately after" Trump's post over the weekend. The BBC's Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson reports from Kyiv, where Ukrainians are facing another winter with electricity outages that leave people without heat, light or even water. text: Rostov Oil Terminal Burns for Third Day After Reported Ukrainian Drone Attack Oct. 12, 2026 exilenova_plus / Telegram A fire at an oil terminal in the southern Russian city of Rostov-on-Don continued to burn for a third day Monday after a reported Ukrainian drone attack over the weekend, according to independent media and Ukrainian monitoring channels. Footage published by Astra and Exilenova+ showed flames and thick smoke rising from the terminal’s fuel storage tanks. The facility, owned by the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery, has a total storage capacity of 60,000 cubic meters and can handle 3.5 million metric tons of petroleum products a year, according to publicly available data. Authorities had not announced that the fire had been extinguished as of midday Monday. The Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova said preliminary information indicated that seven of the terminal’s 12 tanks had burned and another showed signs of fire damage. Footage it published showed blackened tanks alongside others still engulfed in flames. title: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks
text: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks Oct. 12, 2026 Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev. Sergei Kiselev / Moskva News Agency Russia is working on measures to protect data centers from drone attacks after a series of “unprecedented” strikes on tech giant Yandex’s facilities, Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev said Monday. “Yandex faced an unprecedented attack. The Digital Development Ministry, together with the Defense Ministry, is working on the issue of protecting these facilities,” Shadayev told a State Duma committee, according to Interfax. He did not specify what protective measures were under consideration. His comments follow drone attacks on three Yandex data centers in four days that have caused server outages that triggered service disruptions for users. The strikes hit facilities in the Ryazan, Kaluga and Vladimir regions between Thursday and Sunday. The disruptions affected Yandex’s ride-hailing, food delivery and payment services, as well as companies that rely on Yandex Cloud, including online retailer Wildberries and fast-food chain Vkusno i Tochka. news Russia’s Yandex Says Data Center in Vladimir Shut D

title: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees
text: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees Oct. 12, 2026 Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Russia plans to open rehabilitation centers in all eight of its federal districts for soldiers who lost limbs in the war in Ukraine, the Vedomosti business daily reported Monday, citing the state-run Defenders of the Fatherland foundation. The foundation did not give a timetable for opening the facilities. The first center is already operating at a Russian State Social University site in the Moscow region and has served 650 veterans. Deputy Defense Minister Anna Tsivilyova, who has been reported to be President Vladimir Putin’s cousin, said the center teaches former soldiers how to use prosthetic limbs in everyday life. One participant told Vedomosti that veterans learn to walk with prostheses and take part in adaptive sports. But some arrive without a finished prosthesis or with one that no longer works, he said. The man, who was mobilized in 2022 and lost his entire right leg at the front, said he now uses ropes to secure his broken prosthesis to his body so he can practice walking. news After Losing Limbs to War, Russian Amputee Veterans Grapple With Officials’ Empty Promises

title: Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing
text: Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing Oct. 12, 2026 Ukrainian service members launch a drone. REUTERS / Valentyn Ogirenko Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia on Monday of violating an “energy ceasefire” announced by U.S. President Donald Trump, urging Washington to ensure Moscow abides by the agreement as the Kremlin said contacts over a possible truce were ongoing. Russia attacked gas production facilities belonging to Ukraine’s state oil and gas company Naftogaz in the Kharkiv region overnight, causing a fire and damaging critical equipment, the company said Monday. Ukrainian drone attacks, meanwhile, appeared to spare Russian oil refineries overnight after Trump made the surprise announcement that the ceasefire had taken immediate effect. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Monday that contacts over a possible energy ceasefire were continuing. He declined to say whether it would apply only to oil refineries, saying further information would be released in due course. “There were Russian violations of the energy ceasefire announced by President Trump,” Zelensky told a security conference in Warsaw via video

title: Abramovich Aides Backdated Documents to Hide Assets and Avoid Taxes, Report Says
text: Abramovich Aides Backdated Documents to Hide Assets and Avoid Taxes, Report Says Oct. 12, 2026 Roman Abramovich. Sergei Kiselev / Moskva News Agency Aides to Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich, including employees of accounting firm Deloitte Cyprus, allegedly backdated more than 1,000 documents to conceal assets and help his businesses avoid taxes, according to an investigation published Monday. The Guardian and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism examined corporate records from the Cyprus Confidential leak, a collection of more than 500,000 documents that includes internal correspondence. The investigation describes an alleged scheme spanning at least 1999 to 2013, in which documents for more than 100 companies linked to Abramovich were backdated, sometimes by as much as five years. Deloitte Cyprus signed off on financial statements based on those records, the report said. Abramovich and his longtime aide Eugene Tenenbaum deny wrongdoing. The investigation identified Tenenbaum and Demetris Ioannides, the former chairman of Deloitte Cyprus, as central figures in the alleged arrangements. title: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks
text: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks Oct. 12, 2026 Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev. Sergei Kiselev / Moskva News Agency Russia is working on measures to protect data centers from drone attacks after a series of “unprecedented” strikes on tech giant Yandex’s facilities, Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev said Monday. “Yandex faced an unprecedented attack. The Digital Development Ministry, together with the Defense Ministry, is working on the issue of protecting these facilities,” Shadayev told a State Duma committee, according to Interfax. He did not specify what protective measures were under consideration. His comments follow drone attacks on three Yandex data centers in four days that have caused server outages that triggered service disruptions for users. The strikes hit facilities in the Ryazan, Kaluga and Vladimir regions between Thursday and Sunday. The disruptions affected Yandex’s ride-hailing, food delivery and payment services, as well as companies that rely on Yandex Cloud, including online retailer Wildberries and fast-food chain Vkusno i Tochka. news Russia’s Yandex Says Data Center in Vladimir Shut D

title: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees
text: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees Oct. 12, 2026 Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Russia plans to open rehabilitation centers in all eight of its federal districts for soldiers who lost limbs in the war in Ukraine, the Vedomosti business daily reported Monday, citing the state-run Defenders of the Fatherland foundation. The foundation did not give a timetable for opening the facilities. The first center is already operating at a Russian State Social University site in the Moscow region and has served 650 veterans. Deputy Defense Minister Anna Tsivilyova, who has been reported to be President Vladimir Putin’s cousin, said the center teaches former soldiers how to use prosthetic limbs in everyday life. One participant told Vedomosti that veterans learn to walk with prostheses and take part in adaptive sports. But some arrive without a finished prosthesis or with one that no longer works, he said. The man, who was mobilized in 2022 and lost his entire right leg at the front, said he now uses ropes to secure his broken prosthesis to his body so he can practice walking. news After Losing Limbs to War, Russian Amputee Veterans Grapple With Officials’ Empty Promises

title: Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing
text: Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing Oct. 12, 2026 Ukrainian service members launch a drone. REUTERS / Valentyn Ogirenko Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia on Monday of violating an “energy ceasefire” announced by U.S. President Donald Trump, urging Washington to ensure Moscow abides by the agreement as the Kremlin said contacts over a possible truce were ongoing. Russia attacked gas production facilities belonging to Ukraine’s state oil and gas company Naftogaz in the Kharkiv region overnight, causing a fire and damaging critical equipment, the company said Monday. Ukrainian drone attacks, meanwhile, appeared to spare Russian oil refineries overnight after Trump made the surprise announcement that the ceasefire had taken immediate effect. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Monday that contacts over a possible energy ceasefire were continuing. He declined to say whether it would apply only to oil refineries, saying further information would be released in due course. “There were Russian violations of the energy ceasefire announced by President Trump,” Zelensky told a security conference in Warsaw via video

title: Rostov Oil Terminal Burns for Third Day After Reported Ukrainian Drone Attack
text: Rostov Oil Terminal Burns for Third Day After Reported Ukrainian Drone Attack Oct. 12, 2026 exilenova_plus / Telegram A fire at an oil terminal in the southern Russian city of Rostov-on-Don continued to burn for a third day Monday after a reported Ukrainian drone attack over the weekend, according to independent media and Ukrainian monitoring channels. Footage published by Astra and Exilenova+ showed flames and thick smoke rising from the terminal’s fuel storage tanks. The facility, owned by the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery, has a total storage capacity of 60,000 cubic meters and can handle 3.5 million metric tons of petroleum products a year, according to publicly available data. Authorities had not announced that the fire had been extinguished as of midday Monday. The Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova said preliminary information indicated that seven of the terminal’s 12 tanks had burned and another showed signs of fire damage. Footage it published showed blackened tanks alongside others still engulfed in flames. The reported extent of the damage could not be independently confirmed. news Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing Read

title: Tula’s ‘Model Police Officer’ Arrested Over $2K Bribe – Reports
text: Tula’s ‘Model Police Officer’ Arrested Over $2K Bribe – Reports Oct. 12, 2026 Moscow-Live photobank / flickr An award-winning police officer in central Russia’s Tula region has been arrested on suspicion of extorting a 200,000-ruble ($2,400) bribe, the news outlet Ostorozhno Novosti reported Monday. The officer, identified as Yekaterina F., 30, is a deputy supervisor of local district police officers who has served for at least nine years. She reportedly won the regional stage of an Interior Ministry competition honoring district officers in both 2023 and 2024. Investigators allege that she demanded the money from a local resident in exchange for blocking a criminal fraud case against his son involving a forged driver’s license. The man reported the extortion attempt to law enforcement before handing over the money, Ostorozhno Novosti reported. The officer faces up to 12 years in prison if convicted of taking a large bribe through extortion. A Tula judge ordered to place her in pre-trial detention for one month and 29 days. title: Watch: What could Trump's energy ceasefire mean for Ukraine?
text: Watch: What could Trump's energy ceasefire mean for Ukraine? Watch: What could Trump's energy ceasefire mean for Ukraine? Close US President Trump said in a social media post on Sunday that an energy ceasefire had been reached between Ukraine and Russia that was "effective immediately". Ukraine's President Zelensky responded by saying his country is willing to back an energy ceasefire if Russia does the same, adding it could "become a major step toward ending the war". However, Moscow hasn't confirmed its agreement and Zelensky said Russia hit a Ukrainian power plant in Kharkiv "immediately after" Trump's post over the weekend. The BBC's Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson reports from Kyiv, where Ukrainians are facing another winter with electricity outages that leave people without heat, light or even water. title: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says
text: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says Image source, EPA Image caption, Emergency services responded to a Russian drone strike on a residential building in Kharkiv, north-eastern Ukraine on Monday By Olivia Ireland Â and Â Ella Kipling Published 12 October 2026 Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities hours after US President Donald Trump announced the two countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire, Volodymyr Zelensky has said. Despite Trump stating on Sunday the truce would be "effective immediately", the Ukrainian president said Russia had hit "our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities". There were blackouts in the city of Izyum after a Russian strike destroyed power grids, Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform said, while energy and railway infrastructure in western Ukraine was also targeted overnight. On Monday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Ukraine does not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring. What's behind Trump's energy ceasefire claim? title: Why Moscow is staying tight-lipped on Trump's energy ceasefire
text: Why Moscow is staying tight-lipped on Trump's energy ceasefire Image source, Reuters Image caption, Employees of DTEK energy company in Ukraine work to restore power supply following a missile strike in July By Steve Rosenberg BBC Russia editor Published 12 October 2026 On Sunday, US President Donald Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine had agreed a ceasefire on strikes on energy infrastructure "effective immediately". Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky suggested it was "news for me", while Russia has not commented publicly. So who is saying what? Donald Trump says an energy ceasefire has been agreed. Kyiv asks: Has it? text: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says Image source, EPA Image caption, Emergency services responded to a Russian drone strike on a residential building in Kharkiv, north-eastern Ukraine on Monday By Olivia Ireland Â and Â Ella Kipling Published 12 October 2026 Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities hours after US President Donald Trump announced the two countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire, Volodymyr Zelensky has said. Despite Trump stating on Sunday the truce would be "effective immediately", the Ukrainian president said Russia had hit "our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities". There were blackouts in the city of Izyum after a Russian strike destroyed power grids, Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform said, while energy and railway infrastructure in western Ukraine was also targeted overnight. title: Abramovich Aides Backdated Documents to Hide Assets and Avoid Taxes, Report Says
text: Abramovich Aides Backdated Documents to Hide Assets and Avoid Taxes, Report Says Oct. 12, 2026 Roman Abramovich. Sergei Kiselev / Moskva News Agency Aides to Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich, including employees of accounting firm Deloitte Cyprus, allegedly backdated more than 1,000 documents to conceal assets and help his businesses avoid taxes, according to an investigation published Monday. The Guardian and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism examined corporate records from the Cyprus Confidential leak, a collection of more than 500,000 documents that includes internal correspondence. The investigation describes an alleged scheme spanning at least 1999 to 2013, in which documents for more than 100 companies linked to Abramovich were backdated, sometimes by as much as five years. Deloitte Cyprus signed off on financial statements based on those records, the report said. Abramovich and his longtime aide Eugene Tenenbaum deny wrongdoing. The investigation identified Tenenbaum and Demetris Ioannides, the former chairman of Deloitte Cyprus, as central figures in the alleged arrangements. title: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks
text: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks Oct. 12, 2026 Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev. Sergei Kiselev / Moskva News Agency Russia is working on measures to protect data centers from drone attacks after a series of “unprecedented” strikes on tech giant Yandex’s facilities, Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev said Monday. “Yandex faced an unprecedented attack. The Digital Development Ministry, together with the Defense Ministry, is working on the issue of protecting these facilities,” Shadayev told a State Duma committee, according to Interfax. He did not specify what protective measures were under consideration. His comments follow drone attacks on three Yandex data centers in four days that have caused server outages that triggered service disruptions for users. The strikes hit facilities in the Ryazan, Kaluga and Vladimir regions between Thursday and Sunday. The disruptions affected Yandex’s ride-hailing, food delivery and payment services, as well as companies that rely on Yandex Cloud, including online retailer Wildberries and fast-food chain Vkusno i Tochka. news Russia’s Yandex Says Data Center in Vladimir Shut D

title: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees
text: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees Oct. 12, 2026 Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Russia plans to open rehabilitation centers in all eight of its federal districts for soldiers who lost limbs in the war in Ukraine, the Vedomosti business daily reported Monday, citing the state-run Defenders of the Fatherland foundation. The foundation did not give a timetable for opening the facilities. The first center is already operating at a Russian State Social University site in the Moscow region and has served 650 veterans. Deputy Defense Minister Anna Tsivilyova, who has been reported to be President Vladimir Putin’s cousin, said the center teaches former soldiers how to use prosthetic limbs in everyday life. One participant told Vedomosti that veterans learn to walk with prostheses and take part in adaptive sports. But some arrive without a finished prosthesis or with one that no longer works, he said. The man, who was mobilized in 2022 and lost his entire right leg at the front, said he now uses ropes to secure his broken prosthesis to his body so he can practice walking. news After Losing Limbs to War, Russian Amputee Veterans Grapple With Officials’ Empty Promises

title: Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing
text: Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing Oct. 12, 2026 Ukrainian service members launch a drone. REUTERS / Valentyn Ogirenko Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia on Monday of violating an “energy ceasefire” announced by U.S. President Donald Trump, urging Washington to ensure Moscow abides by the agreement as the Kremlin said contacts over a possible truce were ongoing. Russia attacked gas production facilities belonging to Ukraine’s state oil and gas company Naftogaz in the Kharkiv region overnight, causing a fire and damaging critical equipment, the company said Monday. Ukrainian drone attacks, meanwhile, appeared to spare Russian oil refineries overnight after Trump made the surprise announcement that the ceasefire had taken immediate effect. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Monday that contacts over a possible energy ceasefire were continuing. He declined to say whether it would apply only to oil refineries, saying further information would be released in due course. “There were Russian violations of the energy ceasefire announced by President Trump,” Zelensky told a security conference in Warsaw via video

title: Watch: What could Trump's energy ceasefire mean for Ukraine?
text: Watch: What could Trump's energy ceasefire mean for Ukraine? Watch: What could Trump's energy ceasefire mean for Ukraine? Close US President Trump said in a social media post on Sunday that an energy ceasefire had been reached between Ukraine and Russia that was "effective immediately". Ukraine's President Zelensky responded by saying his country is willing to back an energy ceasefire if Russia does the same, adding it could "become a major step toward ending the war". However, Moscow hasn't confirmed its agreement and Zelensky said Russia hit a Ukrainian power plant in Kharkiv "immediately after" Trump's post over the weekend. The BBC's Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson reports from Kyiv, where Ukrainians are facing another winter with electricity outages that leave people without heat, light or even water. REUTERS / Anastasia Barashkova A wave of attacks against the Russian internet giant Yandex has sent shockwaves across the country in recent days and caused major disruptions to daily life. Yandex, often referred to as “Russia’s Google,” provides a range of digital services used by millions of Russians every day. Russian-language media reported widespread outages across the company’s products over the weekend, with people unable to access certain websites and applications. The attacks, which Kyiv says are a retaliation for Russia’s strikes against similar targets, represent a new phase in Ukraine’s air campaign against Russia. title: Abramovich Aides Backdated Documents to Hide Assets and Avoid Taxes, Report Says
text: Abramovich Aides Backdated Documents to Hide Assets and Avoid Taxes, Report Says Oct. 12, 2026 Roman Abramovich. Sergei Kiselev / Moskva News Agency Aides to Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich, including employees of accounting firm Deloitte Cyprus, allegedly backdated more than 1,000 documents to conceal assets and help his businesses avoid taxes, according to an investigation published Monday. The Guardian and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism examined corporate records from the Cyprus Confidential leak, a collection of more than 500,000 documents that includes internal correspondence. The investigation describes an alleged scheme spanning at least 1999 to 2013, in which documents for more than 100 companies linked to Abramovich were backdated, sometimes by as much as five years. Deloitte Cyprus signed off on financial statements based on those records, the report said. Abramovich and his longtime aide Eugene Tenenbaum deny wrongdoing. The investigation identified Tenenbaum and Demetris Ioannides, the former chairman of Deloitte Cyprus, as central figures in the alleged arrangements. title: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks
text: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks Oct. 12, 2026 Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev. Sergei Kiselev / Moskva News Agency Russia is working on measures to protect data centers from drone attacks after a series of “unprecedented” strikes on tech giant Yandex’s facilities, Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev said Monday. “Yandex faced an unprecedented attack. The Digital Development Ministry, together with the Defense Ministry, is working on the issue of protecting these facilities,” Shadayev told a State Duma committee, according to Interfax. He did not specify what protective measures were under consideration. His comments follow drone attacks on three Yandex data centers in four days that have caused server outages that triggered service disruptions for users. The strikes hit facilities in the Ryazan, Kaluga and Vladimir regions between Thursday and Sunday. The disruptions affected Yandex’s ride-hailing, food delivery and payment services, as well as companies that rely on Yandex Cloud, including online retailer Wildberries and fast-food chain Vkusno i Tochka. news Russia’s Yandex Says Data Center in Vladimir Shut D

title: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees
text: Russia Plans Rehab Centers for Ukraine War Amputees Oct. 12, 2026 Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Russia plans to open rehabilitation centers in all eight of its federal districts for soldiers who lost limbs in the war in Ukraine, the Vedomosti business daily reported Monday, citing the state-run Defenders of the Fatherland foundation. The foundation did not give a timetable for opening the facilities. The first center is already operating at a Russian State Social University site in the Moscow region and has served 650 veterans. Deputy Defense Minister Anna Tsivilyova, who has been reported to be President Vladimir Putin’s cousin, said the center teaches former soldiers how to use prosthetic limbs in everyday life. One participant told Vedomosti that veterans learn to walk with prostheses and take part in adaptive sports. But some arrive without a finished prosthesis or with one that no longer works, he said. The man, who was mobilized in 2022 and lost his entire right leg at the front, said he now uses ropes to secure his broken prosthesis to his body so he can practice walking. news After Losing Limbs to War, Russian Amputee Veterans Grapple With Officials’ Empty Promises

title: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says
text: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says Image source, EPA Image caption, Emergency services responded to a Russian drone strike on a residential building in Kharkiv, north-eastern Ukraine on Monday By Olivia Ireland Â and Â Ella Kipling Published 12 October 2026 Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities hours after US President Donald Trump announced the two countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire, Volodymyr Zelensky has said. Despite Trump stating on Sunday the truce would be "effective immediately", the Ukrainian president said Russia had hit "our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities". There were blackouts in the city of Izyum after a Russian strike destroyed power grids, Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform said, while energy and railway infrastructure in western Ukraine was also targeted overnight. On Monday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Ukraine does not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring. What's behind Trump's energy ceasefire claim? title: Rostov Oil Terminal Burns for Third Day After Reported Ukrainian Drone Attack
text: Rostov Oil Terminal Burns for Third Day After Reported Ukrainian Drone Attack Oct. 12, 2026 exilenova_plus / Telegram A fire at an oil terminal in the southern Russian city of Rostov-on-Don continued to burn for a third day Monday after a reported Ukrainian drone attack over the weekend, according to independent media and Ukrainian monitoring channels. Footage published by Astra and Exilenova+ showed flames and thick smoke rising from the terminal’s fuel storage tanks. The facility, owned by the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery, has a total storage capacity of 60,000 cubic meters and can handle 3.5 million metric tons of petroleum products a year, according to publicly available data. Authorities had not announced that the fire had been extinguished as of midday Monday. The Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova said preliminary information indicated that seven of the terminal’s 12 tanks had burned and another showed signs of fire damage. Footage it published showed blackened tanks alongside others still engulfed in flames. The reported extent of the damage could not be independently confirmed. news Zelensky Accuses Russia of Breaking Energy Ceasefire as Kremlin Says Talks Ongoing Read

title: Tula’s ‘Model Police Officer’ Arrested Over $2K Bribe – Reports
text: Tula’s ‘Model Police Officer’ Arrested Over $2K Bribe – Reports Oct. 12, 2026 Moscow-Live photobank / flickr An award-winning police officer in central Russia’s Tula region has been arrested on suspicion of extorting a 200,000-ruble ($2,400) bribe, the news outlet Ostorozhno Novosti reported Monday. The officer, identified as Yekaterina F., 30, is a deputy supervisor of local district police officers who has served for at least nine years. She reportedly won the regional stage of an Interior Ministry competition honoring district officers in both 2023 and 2024. Investigators allege that she demanded the money from a local resident in exchange for blocking a criminal fraud case against his son involving a forged driver’s license. The man reported the extortion attempt to law enforcement before handing over the money, Ostorozhno Novosti reported. The officer faces up to 12 years in prison if convicted of taking a large bribe through extortion. A Tula judge ordered to place her in pre-trial detention for one month and 29 days.
